artworks.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha
artworks.description: Rubens' Prado sketch for the Torre de la Parada: the flood survivors cast stones that become a new human race — Ovid's Greek deluge as Baroque energy after the waters fall.

artworks.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha
artworks.description: Castiglione's Denver canvas isolates the couple in a rocky waste as they throw their 'mother's bones' — the stones of earth that rise as men and women after Zeus' flood.

artworks.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha
artworks.description: Solis's Metamorphoses woodcut freezes the oracle's command: husband and wife hurl stones over their shoulders while new bodies form — the print that carried Greece's Noah story through Renaissance editions.

popCulture.title: Deucalion
popCulture.description: Deucalion and Pyrrha's flood endures as Greece's Noah story — stones thrown over the shoulder that become a new humankind.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 1 makes Deucalion and Pyrrha the survivors who repopulate the world from stones — the Greek flood as Rome's foundational metamorphosis.
